https://ksp.etri.re.kr/ksp/plan-report/r.description: 디지털 전환 시대 통신망 투자의 중요성은 높아지고 있으나, 시장 환경 변화로 통신사업자의 투자 유인은 약화되고 있는 상황이다. 본 보고서는 소비자 관점에서 디지털 콘텐츠 생태계의 순환 구조를 살펴보고, 이를 기반으로 통신사업자 투자 유인 제고를 위한 시사점을 도출하고자 하였다. 이를 위해, 설문조사 데이터를 기반으로 ① 네트워크 품질과 연결된 개별 QoE 요소의 보장이 OTT 미디어 이용자 가치로 이어지는지 여부와, ② OTT 미디어에 따른 데이터 추가 수요가 이동통신서비스 요금제 선택에 영향을 미치는지 여부를 실증 분석하였다. 분석 결과, 네트워크 품질과 연관된 OTT 미디어 시청의 QoE 요소가 이용자 가치로 이어지는 것을 확인하였으나, OTT 미디어 시청으로 인한 데이터 추가 수요가 요금제 변경을 통한 수익 증대로 연결되는 효과는 제한적인 것으로 나타났다. 따라서, 지속가능한 네트워크 투자 유인을 제고하기 위해서는 현재의 선순환 구조에서의 구조적 제약을 완화할 수 있는 다양한 이해관계자 간의 협력 등 대안적 접근의 모색이 필요할 것으로 보인다.

https://ksp.etri.re.kr/ksp/plan-report/r.description: 최근 AI가 미디어의 새로운 생산·소비 주체로 부상하면서, 인간 중심으로 전개되어 온 미디어 생태계가 구조적 전환 국면에 진입하고 있다. 특히 AI는 콘텐츠 제작, 분석, 유통, 의사결정 등 전 과정에서 미디어 기능을 고도화하는 핵심 동력으로 자리 잡으며, 관련 사례를 빠르게 확산시키고 있다. 반면, 미디어가 AI의 학습과 추론을 직접적으로 지원하는 인프라로서 어떻게 설계되고 운영되어야 하는지에 대한 개념적 논의는 충분히 제시되지 못한 상황이다. 본 연구는 이러한 변화의 흐름을 반영하여, AI의 개발과 활용 전 과정을 매개하는 미디어 구조를 ‘Media for AI’로 정의하고, 산업별 실증 사례 분석을 통해 구체화한다. 나아가 이러한 탐색 과정을 통해 AI를 실질적으로 지원하는 미디어 기술 요소를 식별하고, 향후 AI 경쟁력을 좌우할 미디어의 발전 방향과 전략적 함의를 제시한다.
https://ksp.etri.re.kr/ksp/plan-report/r.title: AI 시대 미디어의 새로운 기능과 역할: Media for AI

https://ksp.etri.re.kr/ksp/plan-report/r.description: 최근 디지털 전환, 탄소중립, 기술 패권 경쟁 등 글로벌 환경 변화 속에서 기술정책은 단순한 연구개발 지원을 넘어 경제·사회·안보를 포괄하는 국가 전략 영역으로 확대되고 있다. 본 연구는 기술정책과 혁신전략의 개념적 구조와 상호 관계를 분석하고, 국내외 연구 동향과 주요국 정책 사례를 비교하여 정책 변화의 특징을 도출하는 것을 목적으로 한다. 이를 위해 문헌 분석과 텍스트 마이닝 기반 토픽 분석, 국가별 정책 비교 분석을 수행하였다. 분석 결과 기술정책 및 혁신전략의 주요 이슈는 인공지능과 디지털 전환, 산업 경쟁력 강화, 탄소중립, 기술안보와 공급망, 국가혁신시스템 거버넌스, 기술 예측 등으로 나타났다. 또한 글로벌 기술정책은 정책 목표의 다층화, 정책 수단의 시스템화, 거버넌스 확장 방향으로 발전하고 있음을 확인하였다. 연구 결과를 바탕으로 한국 기술정책의 발전을 위한 통합적 정책 설계와 예측 기반 정책체계 구축 등의 정책적 시사점을 제시하였다.

https://ksp.etri.re.kr/ksp/plan-report/r.description: AI 경쟁은 이제 학습 중심의 확장 국면을 넘어 추론 중심의 운영 경쟁이 본격화되는 변곡점에 진입하고 있다. 기술 경쟁의 핵심도 더 큰 모델의 선제적 확보에서, 대규모 추론을 더 낮은 비용과 더 높은 효율로 안정적으로 운영하는 구조의 설계로 빠르게 이동하고 있다. 이 과정에서 알고리즘 구조는 연산, 저장, 데이터 이동 방식을 규정함으로써 시스템·인프라·산업구조 전반을 좌우하는 핵심 변수로 부상하고 있다. 추론 중심 경쟁이 촉발한 구조적 전환은 알고리즘 구조 변화에서 출발해 가치사슬과 산업구조 재편으로 확산되는 과정으로 나타난다. 추론 중심 AI로의 전환과 알고리즘 구조 변화는 알고리즘·시스템·인프라 공동설계를 가속하고, 이는 다시 AI 가치사슬 재편과 운영 구조 경쟁을 거쳐 산업구조 변화와 기술패권 경쟁 재편으로 이어진다. 본 보고서에서는 이러한 흐름에 따라 1장에서 기술 경쟁의 전환, 2장에서 알고리즘 구조 혁신, 3장에서 시스템·인프라 구조 전환, 4장에서 기술패권 경쟁 재편의 산업·정책적 함의와 전략을 살펴본다.

https://ksp.etri.re.kr/ksp/plan-report/r.description: 정체된 디스플레이 산업에 대한 새로운 기회로 Physical AI 시대를 주목하여 향후의 활용 방향성과 이를 위한 추진 과제를 도출하였다. 디스플레이 시장의 성장 정체와 함께 국가 간 치열한 경쟁 속에서 Physical AI는 정체된 디스플레이 산업에 새로운 수요를 창출할 수 있는 중요한 전환점으로 판단되는 가운데, 기존 디지털 AI에서는 디스플레이가 정보와 영상을 출력하는 주변 장치에 가까웠으나, Physical AI에서는 인간·AI·물리적 환경을 연결하는 핵심 매체로 역할이 확대될 전망이기 때문에, 디스플레이는 기존의 ‘보는 화면’에서 ‘감지하고 판단하며 소통하는 지능형 인터페이스’로 진화(인지강화형 디스플레이, AI 내재형 디스플레이)해야 한다. 이를 위해서는 프리폼 감각 인터페이스와 System-on-Panel을 국가 차원의 중장기 도전형 R&D 과제로 추진하고, 디스플레이 기업과 로봇·모빌리티·XR·의료기기 기업이 공동으로 참여하는 수요 연계형 R&BD 체계를 구축해야 한다.

https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.title: KDI 경제동향 2026. 3

https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.description: ■ 완만한 경기 개선 흐름을 보여왔던 우리 경제는 중동 전쟁으로 경기 하방 위험이 확대 되는 모습 ○ 내수가 완만하게 개선되는 가운데 수출도 반도체를 중심으로 높은 증가세를 나타냄. - 2월 중 소비 개선 흐름이 지속되는 가운데 반도체를 중심으로 설비투자도 높은 증가세를 나타내었으며, 건설투자 감소세는 다소 완화 - 생산 측면에서도 서비스업의 양호한 증가세가 유지되는 가운데, 반도체 생산이 급증하면서 제조업의 증가세도 확대 ○ 그러나 3월 들어 중동 전쟁에 따른 국제유가 급등, 글로벌 공급망 불안 등으로 경기 하방 위험이 확대되는 모습 - 석유류가격이 대폭 상승하였으며, 향후 원유와 밀접한 부문을 중심으로 물가상승세가 확대될 가능성 - 아울러 세계 경기 불안으로 수출 여건이 다소 악화된 가운데, 불확실성 확대로 투자 회복도 제약될 가능성 - 이에 따라 기업심리지수와 소비자심리지수도 하락
https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.title: KDI 경제동향 2026. 4

https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.description: ■ 최근 우리 경제 는 반도체 수출이 대폭 증가하는 가운데, 서비스업도 개선되면서 경기 회복세를 보임. ○ 수출이 반도체를 중심으로 높은 증가율을 기록하고, 내수가 개선세를 유지 - 반도체 호조세로 수출가격이 급등한 가운데, 수출물량도 비교적 높은 증가세를 보임. - 건설투자가 다소 부진하나, 설비투자의 높은 증가세가 유지된 가운데, 소비 개선 흐름도 지속 ○ 중동 전쟁 지속에 따른 경기 하방 위험이 존재 - 원유 수송 차질로 생산 비용이 증가함에 따라 소비자물가 상승세가 확대되었으며, 기대인플레이션도 상승하는 모습
https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.title: KDI 경제동향 2026. 5

https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.description: ■ 최근 우리 경제 는 중동 전쟁에 따른 경기 하방 위험에도 불구하고, 반도체 호황을 중심으로 완만한 개선세 는 유지 ○ 내수가 완만하게 개선되는 가운데 수출은 반도체를 중심으로 높은 증가세를 이어감. - 건설투자가 부진하나, 소비의 완만한 개선 흐름이 지속되는 가운데 설비투자가 반도체를 중심으로 높은 증가세를 보임. - 반도체 호조세로 수출가격이 급등한 가운데 수출물량도 양호한 증가세를 이어감. ○ 그러나 중동 전쟁으로 원유 수송 차질이 지속되며 경기 하방 위험이 상존 - 고유가 지속으로 소비자물가 상승률이 확대된 가운데, 생산 비용도 상승함. - 이와 함께, 원유 공급 차질로 석유정제 생산과 석유제품 수출물량이 감소하는 등 중동 전쟁의 부정적 영향이 일부 가시화되는 모습
https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.title: KDI 경제동향 2026. 6

https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.description: ■ 우리 경제 는 제조업생산이 조정되었으나, 반도체 수출과 서비스업 호조에 힘입어 완만한 개선 흐름을 유지 ○ 수출은 견조한 AI 관련 수요에 힘입어 반도체 등 ICT 품목을 중심으로 높은 증가세를 지속하였으며, 반도체 관련 투자도 양호한 흐름을 이어감. - 반도체 수출물량의 증가세는 조정되었으나, 가격 상승세로 수출금액 기준으로는 호조세 유지 ○ 서비스업생산은 금융보험업과 전문과학기술서비스업을 중심으로 높은 상승세를 이어가며 전산업생산의 증가세를 뒷받침 - 소비가 완만한 증가세를 이어간 가운데, 이와 밀접한 서비스업생산도 개선 ○ 다만, 제조업생산은 반도체의 높았던 증가세가 조정되는 가운데, 여타 부문도 미약한 흐름을 보이며 소폭 감소
https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.title: KDI 경제동향 2026. 7

https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.description: ■ 우리 경제 는 반도체 관련 부문을 중심으로 개선세가 확대되는 모습 ○ 반도체를 중심으로 수출과 설비투자가 높은 증가세를 보인 가운데, 소비도 내구재를 중심으로 증가폭이 확대 ○ 전산업생산은 서비스업의 양호한 흐름이 이어진 가운데 제조업도 반등하면서 비교적 높은 증가율을 기록 - 서비스업생산이 금융 및 보험업, 전문·과학 및 기술서비스업을 중심으로 높은 증가세를 지속하였으며, 제조업생산도 자동차, 기계장비 등 대다수 업종에서 반등 ○ 다만, 미국의 관세 조치와 중동 정세 불안이 지속되는 가운데, 물가상승률이 아직 높은 수준을 보이고 고용 여건도 둔화되는 등 대내외 불확실성이 상존
https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.title: KDI 경제동향 2026. 8

https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.description: ■ 우리 경제 는 AI 관련 투자와 밀접한 부문을 중심으로 개선 흐름을 유지 ○ 국내외 AI 인프라 투자 확대에 힘입어 수출과 설비투자가 높은 증가세를 이어간 가운데, 관련 부문의 제조업생산도 증가를 지속 - 수출과 설비투자가 반도체를 중심으로 높은 증가세를 지속하였으며, 금속가공, 전기장비, 기계장비 등 AI 투자와 관련된 부문의 생산도 비교적 양호한 모습 ○ 그럼에도 불구하고 경기 개선이 가계 전반의 소득으로 충분히 파급되지 못하면서 소비 개선세는 완만한 모습 - 서비스업생산도 소비와 밀접한 도소매, 숙박 및 음식점 등의 업종을 중심으로 높았던 증가세가 조정되는 모습 ○ 한편, 중동 정세 불안과 미국의 통상정책을 둘러싼 불확실성은 여전히 높은 수준
https://www.kdi.re.kr/research/monTrends.title: KDI 경제동향 2026. 9

candidates.title: Customizing GPT-3 for your application

candidates.description: As part of our effort to support and develop AI talent, we’re excited to announce the OpenAI Residency.
candidates.title: OpenAI Residency

candidates.description: Wider availability made possible by safety progress.
candidates.title: OpenAI’s API now available with no waitlist

candidates.description: We’ve trained a system that solves grade school math problems with nearly twice the accuracy of a fine-tuned GPT-3 model. It solves about 90% as many problems as real kids: a small sample of 9-12 year olds scored 60% on a test from our dataset, while our system scored 55% on those same problems.
candidates.title: Solving math word problems

candidates.description: Scaling human oversight of AI systems for tasks that are difficult to evaluate.
candidates.title: Summarizing books with human feedback

candidates.description: Today, we’re excited to announce the appointment of Helen Toner to our board of directors.
candidates.title: Helen Toner joins OpenAI’s board of directors
TruthfulQA: Measuring how models mimic human falsehoods

candidates.description: We’ve created an improved version of OpenAI Codex, our AI system that translates natural language to code, and we are releasing it through our API in private beta starting today.
candidates.title: OpenAI Codex

candidates.description: We’re releasing Triton 1.0, an open-source Python-like programming language which enables researchers with no CUDA experience to write highly efficient GPU code—most of the time on par with what an expert would be able to produce.
candidates.title: Introducing Triton: Open-source GPU programming for neural networks
Evaluating large language models trained on code

candidates.description: Our latest research finds we can improve language model behavior with respect to specific behavioral values by fine-tuning on a small, curated dataset.
candidates.title: Improving language model behavior by training on a curated dataset

candidates.description: We’re proud to announce that the 2021 class of OpenAI Scholars has completed our six-month mentorship program and have produced an open-source research project with stipends and support from OpenAI.
candidates.title: OpenAI Scholars 2021: Final projects

candidates.description: OpenAI is committed to developing general-purpose artificial intelligence that benefits all humanity, and we believe that achieving our goal requires expertise in public policy as well as technology. So, we’re delighted to announce that Congressman Will Hurd has joined our board of directors.
candidates.title: Will Hurd joins OpenAI’s board of directors

candidates.description: Over 300 applications are delivering GPT-3–powered search, conversation, text completion, and other advanced AI features through our API.
candidates.title: GPT-3 powers the next generation of apps

candidates.description: We’ve discovered neurons in CLIP that respond to the same concept whether presented literally, symbolically, or conceptually. This may explain CLIP’s accuracy in classifying surprising visual renditions of concepts, and is also an important step toward understanding the associations and biases that CLIP and similar models learn.
candidates.title: Multimodal neurons in artificial neural networks
Understanding the capabilities, limitations, and societal impact of large language models

candidates.description: We’ve scaled Kubernetes clusters to 7,500 nodes, producing a scalable infrastructure for large models like GPT-3, CLIP, and DALL·E, but also for rapid small-scale iterative research such as Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models.
candidates.title: Scaling Kubernetes to 7,500 nodes

candidates.description: We’ve trained a neural network called DALL·E that creates images from text captions for a wide range of concepts expressible in natural language.
candidates.title: DALL·E: Creating images from text

candidates.description: We’re introducing a neural network called CLIP which efficiently learns visual concepts from natural language supervision. CLIP can be applied to any visual classification benchmark by simply providing the names of the visual categories to be recognized, similar to the “zero-shot” capabilities of GPT-2 and GPT-3.
candidates.title: CLIP: Connecting text and images

candidates.description: It’s been a year of dramatic change and growth at OpenAI.
candidates.title: Organizational update from OpenAI

candidates.description: OpenAI has agreed to license GPT-3 to Microsoft for their own products and services.
candidates.title: OpenAI licenses GPT-3 technology to Microsoft
Generative language modeling for automated theorem proving

candidates.description: We’ve applied reinforcement learning from human feedback to train language models that are better at summarization.
candidates.title: Learning to summarize with human feedback

candidates.description: Our third class of OpenAI Scholars presented their final projects at virtual Demo Day, showcasing their research results from over the past five months.
candidates.title: OpenAI Scholars 2020: Final projects

candidates.description: We’re excited to announce that OpenAI is co-organizing two NeurIPS 2020 competitions with AIcrowd, Carnegie Mellon University, and DeepMind, using Procgen Benchmark and MineRL.
candidates.title: Procgen and MineRL Competitions

candidates.description: We find that, just as a large transformer model trained on language can generate coherent text, the same exact model trained on pixel sequences can generate coherent image completions and samples. By establishing a correlation between sample quality and image classification accuracy, we show that our best generative model also contains features competitive with top convolutional nets in the unsupervised setting.
candidates.title: Image GPT

candidates.description: We’re releasing an API for accessing new AI models developed by OpenAI.
candidates.title: OpenAI API
Language models are few-shot learners

candidates.description: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012 the amount of compute needed to train a neural net to the same performance on ImageNet classification has been decreasing by a factor of 2 every 16 months. Compared to 2012, it now takes 44 times less compute to train a neural network to the level of AlexNet (by contrast, Moore’s Law would yield an 11x cost improvement over this period). Our results suggest that for AI tasks with high levels of recent investment, algorithmic progress has yielded more gains than classical hardware efficiency.
candidates.title: AI and efficiency

candidates.description: We’re introducing Jukebox, a neural net that generates music, including rudimentary singing, as raw audio in a variety of genres and artist styles. We’re releasing the model weights and code, along with a tool to explore the generated samples.
candidates.title: Jukebox

candidates.description: We’ve contributed to a multi-stakeholder report by 58 co-authors at 30 organizations, including the Centre for the Future of Intelligence, Mila, Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society, Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences, and Center for Security and Emerging Technologies. This report describes 10 mechanisms to improve the verifiability of claims made about AI systems. Developers can use these tools to provide evidence that AI systems are safe, secure, fair, or privacy-preserving. Users, policymakers, and civil society can use these tools to evaluate AI developme
candidates.title: Improving verifiability in AI development

candidates.description: We’re introducing OpenAI Microscope, a collection of visualizations of every significant layer and neuron of eight vision “model organisms” which are often studied in interpretability. Microscope makes it easier to analyze the features that form inside these neural networks, and we hope it will help the research community as we move towards understanding these complicated systems.
candidates.title: OpenAI Microscope

candidates.description: We are standardizing OpenAI’s deep learning framework on PyTorch.
candidates.title: OpenAI standardizes on PyTorch
Scaling laws for neural language models
Dota 2 with large scale deep reinforcement learning

candidates.description: We show that the double descent phenomenon occurs in CNNs, ResNets, and transformers: performance first improves, then gets worse, and then improves again with increasing model size, data size, or training time. This effect is often avoided through careful regularization. While this behavior appears to be fairly universal, we don’t yet fully understand why it happens, and view further study of this phenomenon as an important research direction.
candidates.title: Deep double descent

candidates.description: We’re releasing Procgen Benchmark, 16 simple-to-use procedurally-generated environments which provide a direct measure of how quickly a reinforcement learning agent learns generalizable skills.
candidates.title: Procgen Benchmark

candidates.description: We’re releasing Safety Gym, a suite of environments and tools for measuring progress towards reinforcement learning agents that respect safety constraints while training.
candidates.title: Safety Gym
Benchmarking safe exploration in deep reinforcement learning

candidates.description: As the final model release of GPT-2’s staged release, we’re releasing the largest version (1.5B parameters) of GPT-2 along with code and model weights to facilitate detection of outputs of GPT-2 models. While there have been larger language models released since August, we’ve continued with our original staged release plan in order to provide the community with a test case of a full staged release process. We hope that this test case will be useful to developers of future powerful models, and we’re actively continuing the conversation with the AI community on responsible publication.
candidates.title: GPT-2: 1.5B release

candidates.description: We’ve trained a pair of neural networks to solve the Rubik’s Cube with a human-like robot hand. The neural networks are trained entirely in simulation, using the same reinforcement learning code as OpenAI Five paired with a new technique called Automatic Domain Randomization (ADR). The system can handle situations it never saw during training, such as being prodded by a stuffed giraffe. This shows that reinforcement learning isn’t just a tool for virtual tasks, but can solve physical-world problems requiring unprecedented dexterity.
candidates.title: Solving Rubik’s Cube with a robot hand

candidates.description: We are now accepting applications for our third class of OpenAI Scholars.
candidates.title: OpenAI Scholars 2020: Applications open

candidates.description: We’ve fine-tuned the 774M parameter GPT-2 language model using human feedback for various tasks, successfully matching the preferences of the external human labelers, though those preferences did not always match our own. Specifically, for summarization tasks the labelers preferred sentences copied wholesale from the input (we’d only asked them to ensure accuracy), so our models learned to copy. Summarization required 60k human labels; simpler tasks which continue text in various styles required only 5k. Our motivation is to move safety techniques closer to the general task of “machines talkin
candidates.title: Fine-tuning GPT-2 from human preferences

candidates.description: We’ve observed agents discovering progressively more complex tool use while playing a simple game of hide-and-seek. Through training in our new simulated hide-and-seek environment, agents build a series of six distinct strategies and counterstrategies, some of which we did not know our environment supported. The self-supervised emergent complexity in this simple environment further suggests that multi-agent co-adaptation may one day produce extremely complex and intelligent behavior.
candidates.title: Emergent tool use from multi-agent interaction

candidates.description: We’ve developed a method to assess whether a neural network classifier can reliably defend against adversarial attacks not seen during training. Our method yields a new metric, UAR (Unforeseen Attack Robustness), which evaluates the robustness of a single model against an unanticipated attack, and highlights the need to measure performance across a more diverse range of unforeseen attacks.
candidates.title: Testing robustness against unforeseen adversaries

candidates.description: We’re releasing the 774 million parameter GPT-2 language model after the release of our small 124M model in February, staged release of our medium 355M model in May, and subsequent research with partners and the AI community into the model’s potential for misuse and societal benefit. We’re also releasing an open-source legal agreement to make it easier for organizations to initiate model-sharing partnerships with each other, and are publishing a technical report about our experience in coordinating with the wider AI research community on publication norms.
candidates.title: GPT-2: 6-month follow-up

candidates.description: At OpenAI, each Thursday is Learning Day: a day where employees have the option to self-study technical skills that will make them better at their job but which aren’t being learned from daily work.
candidates.title: Learning Day

candidates.description: Microsoft is investing $1 billion in OpenAI to support us building artificial general intelligence (AGI) with widely distributed economic benefits. We’re partnering to develop a hardware and software platform within Microsoft Azure which will scale to AGI. We’ll jointly develop new Azure AI supercomputing technologies, and Microsoft will become our exclusive cloud provider—so we’ll be working hard together to further extend Microsoft Azure’s capabilities in large-scale AI systems.
candidates.title: Microsoft invests in and partners with OpenAI to support us building beneficial AGI

candidates.description: We’ve written a policy research paper identifying four strategies that can be used today to improve the likelihood of long-term industry cooperation on safety norms in AI: communicating risks and benefits, technical collaboration, increased transparency, and incentivizing standards. Our analysis shows that industry cooperation on safety will be instrumental in ensuring that AI systems are safe and beneficial, but competitive pressures could lead to a collective action problem, potentially causing AI companies to under-invest in safety. We hope these strategies will encourage greater cooperatio
candidates.title: Why responsible AI development needs cooperation on safety

candidates.description: We hosted the first OpenAI Robotics Symposium on April 27, 2019.
candidates.title: OpenAI Robotics Symposium 2019

candidates.description: Our second class of OpenAI Scholars has concluded, with all eight scholars producing an exciting final project showcased at Scholars Demo Day at OpenAI.
candidates.title: OpenAI Scholars 2019: Final projects

candidates.description: Our second class of OpenAI Fellows has wrapped up, with each Fellow going from a machine learning beginner to core OpenAI contributor in the course of a 6-month apprenticeship. We are currently reviewing applications on a rolling basis for our next round of OpenAI Fellows Summer 2019.
candidates.title: OpenAI Fellows Fall 2018: Final projects
Transfer of adversarial robustness between perturbation types

candidates.description: We’ve created MuseNet, a deep neural network that can generate 4-minute musical compositions with 10 different instruments, and can combine styles from country to Mozart to the Beatles. MuseNet was not explicitly programmed with our understanding of music, but instead discovered patterns of harmony, rhythm, and style by learning to predict the next token in hundreds of thousands of MIDI files. MuseNet uses the same general-purpose unsupervised technology as GPT-2, a large-scale transformer model trained to predict the next token in a sequence, whether audio or text.
candidates.title: MuseNet

candidates.description: We’ve developed the Sparse Transformer, a deep neural network which sets new records at predicting what comes next in a sequence—whether text, images, or sound. It uses an algorithmic improvement of the attention mechanism to extract patterns from sequences 30x longer than possible previously.
candidates.title: Generative modeling with sparse transformers

candidates.description: OpenAI Five is the first AI to beat the world champions in an esports game, having won two back-to-back games versus the world champion Dota 2 team, OG, at Finals this weekend. Both OpenAI Five and DeepMind’s AlphaStar had previously beaten good pros privately but lost their live pro matches, making this also the first time an AI has beaten esports pros on livestream.
candidates.title: OpenAI Five defeats Dota 2 world champions

candidates.description: We’ll be holding our final live event for OpenAI Five at 11:30am PT on April 13.
candidates.title: OpenAI Five Finals

candidates.description: We’ve made progress towards stable and scalable training of energy-based models (EBMs) resulting in better sample quality and generalization ability than existing models. Generation in EBMs spends more compute to continually refine its answers and doing so can generate samples competitive with GANs at low temperatures, while also having mode coverage guarantees of likelihood-based models. We hope these findings stimulate further research into this promising class of models.
candidates.title: Implicit generation and generalization methods for energy-based models

candidates.description: Our class of eight scholars (out of 550 applicants) brings together collective expertise in literature, philosophy, cell biology, statistics, economics, quantum physics, and business innovation.
candidates.title: OpenAI Scholars 2019: Meet our Scholars

candidates.description: We’ve created OpenAI LP, a new “capped-profit” company that allows us to rapidly increase our investments in compute and talent while including checks and balances to actualize our mission.
candidates.title: OpenAI LP

candidates.description: We’ve created activation atlases (in collaboration with Google researchers), a new technique for visualizing what interactions between neurons can represent. As AI systems are deployed in increasingly sensitive contexts, having a better understanding of their internal decision-making processes will let us identify weaknesses and investigate failures.
candidates.title: Introducing Activation Atlases

candidates.description: We’re releasing a Neural MMO, a massively multiagent game environment for reinforcement learning agents. Our platform supports a large, variable number of agents within a persistent and open-ended task. The inclusion of many agents and species leads to better exploration, divergent niche formation, and greater overall competence.
candidates.title: Neural MMO: A massively multiagent game environment

candidates.description: On February 2, we held our first Spinning Up Workshop as part of our new education initiative at OpenAI.
candidates.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL: Workshop review

candidates.description: We’ve written a paper arguing that long-term AI safety research needs social scientists to ensure AI alignment algorithms succeed when actual humans are involved. Properly aligning advanced AI systems with human values requires resolving many uncertainties related to the psychology of human rationality, emotion, and biases. The aim of this paper is to spark further collaboration between machine learning and social science researchers, and we plan to hire social scientists to work on this full time at OpenAI.
candidates.title: AI safety needs social scientists

candidates.description: We’ve trained a large-scale unsupervised language model which generates coherent paragraphs of text, achieves state-of-the-art performance on many language modeling benchmarks, and performs rudimentary reading comprehension, machine translation, question answering, and summarization—all without task-specific training.
candidates.title: Better language models and their implications
Computational limitations in robust classification and win-win results

candidates.description: Our first cohort of OpenAI Fellows has concluded, with each Fellow going from a machine learning beginner to core OpenAI contributor in the course of a 6-month apprenticeship.
candidates.title: OpenAI Fellows Summer 2018: Final projects

candidates.description: We’ve discovered that the gradient noise scale, a simple statistical metric, predicts the parallelizability of neural network training on a wide range of tasks. Since complex tasks tend to have noisier gradients, increasingly large batch sizes are likely to become useful in the future, removing one potential limit to further growth of AI systems. More broadly, these results show that neural network training need not be considered a mysterious art, but can be rigorized and systematized.
candidates.title: How AI training scales

candidates.description: We’re releasing CoinRun, a training environment which provides a metric for an agent’s ability to transfer its experience to novel situations and has already helped clarify a longstanding puzzle in reinforcement learning. CoinRun strikes a desirable balance in complexity: the environment is simpler than traditional platformer games like Sonic the Hedgehog but still poses a worthy generalization challenge for state of the art algorithms.
candidates.title: Quantifying generalization in reinforcement learning

candidates.description: We’re releasing Spinning Up in Deep RL, an educational resource designed to let anyone learn to become a skilled practitioner in deep reinforcement learning. Spinning Up consists of crystal-clear examples of RL code, educational exercises, documentation, and tutorials.
candidates.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL

candidates.description: We’ve developed an energy-based model that can quickly learn to identify and generate instances of concepts, such as near, above, between, closest, and furthest, expressed as sets of 2d points. Our model learns these concepts after only five demonstrations. We also show cross-domain transfer: we use concepts learned in a 2d particle environment to solve tasks on a 3-dimensional physics-based robot.
candidates.title: Learning concepts with energy functions
Plan online, learn offline: Efficient learning and exploration via model-based control

candidates.description: We’ve developed Random Network Distillation (RND), a prediction-based method for encouraging reinforcement learning agents to explore their environments through curiosity, which for the first time exceeds average human performance on Montezuma’s Revenge.
candidates.title: Reinforcement learning with prediction-based rewards

candidates.description: We’re proposing an AI safety technique called iterated amplification that lets us specify complicated behaviors and goals that are beyond human scale, by demonstrating how to decompose a task into simpler sub-tasks, rather than by providing labeled data or a reward function. Although this idea is in its very early stages and we have only completed experiments on simple toy algorithmic domains, we’ve decided to present it in its preliminary state because we think it could prove to be a scalable approach to AI safety.
candidates.title: Learning complex goals with iterated amplification

candidates.description: We are now accepting applications for our second cohort of OpenAI Scholars, a program where we provide 6–10 stipends and mentorship to individuals from underrepresented groups to study deep learning full-time for 3 months and open-source a project.
candidates.title: OpenAI Scholars 2019: Applications open

candidates.description: We are now accepting applications for OpenAI Fellows and Interns for 2019.
candidates.title: OpenAI Fellows Winter 2019 & Interns Summer 2019
FFJORD: Free-form continuous dynamics for scalable reversible generative models

candidates.description: Our first cohort of OpenAI Scholars has now completed the program.
candidates.title: OpenAI Scholars 2018: Final projects

candidates.description: OpenAI Five lost two games against top Dota 2 players at The International in Vancouver this week, maintaining a good chance of winning for the first 20–35 minutes of both games.
candidates.title: The International 2018: Results
Large-scale study of curiosity-driven learning

candidates.description: Yesterday, OpenAI Five won a best-of-three against a team of 99.95th percentile Dota players: Blitz, Cap, Fogged, Merlini, and MoonMeander—four of whom have played Dota professionally—in front of a live audience and 100,000 concurrent livestream viewers.
candidates.title: OpenAI Five Benchmark: Results

candidates.description: We’ve trained a human-like robot hand to manipulate physical objects with unprecedented dexterity.
candidates.title: Learning dexterity
Variational option discovery algorithms

candidates.description: Our first class of OpenAI Scholars is underway, and you can now follow along as this group of experienced software developers becomes machine learning practitioners.
candidates.title: OpenAI Scholars 2018: Meet our Scholars

candidates.description: The OpenAI Five Benchmark match is now over!
candidates.title: OpenAI Five Benchmark

candidates.description: We introduce Glow, a reversible generative model which uses invertible 1x1 convolutions. It extends previous work on reversible generative models and simplifies the architecture. Our model can generate realistic high resolution images, supports efficient sampling, and discovers features that can be used to manipulate attributes of data. We’re releasing code for the model and an online visualization tool so people can explore and build on these results.
candidates.title: Glow: Better reversible generative models

candidates.description: We’ve trained an agent to achieve a high score of 74,500 on Montezuma’s Revenge from a single human demonstration, better than any previously published result. Our algorithm is simple: the agent plays a sequence of games starting from carefully chosen states from the demonstration, and learns from them by optimizing the game score using PPO, the same reinforcement learning algorithm that underpins OpenAI Five.
candidates.title: Learning Montezuma’s Revenge from a single demonstration

candidates.description: Our team of five neural networks, OpenAI Five, has started to defeat amateur human teams at Dota 2.
candidates.title: OpenAI Five

candidates.description: The first run of our Retro Contest—exploring the development of algorithms that can generalize from previous experience—is now complete.
candidates.title: Retro Contest: Results
Learning policy representations in multiagent systems

candidates.description: We’ve obtained state-of-the-art results on a suite of diverse language tasks with a scalable, task-agnostic system, which we’re also releasing. Our approach is a combination of two existing ideas: transformers and unsupervised pre-training. These results provide a convincing example that pairing supervised learning methods with unsupervised pre-training works very well; this is an idea that many have explored in the past, and we hope our result motivates further research into applying this idea on larger and more diverse datasets.
candidates.title: Improving language understanding with unsupervised learning
GamePad: A learning environment for theorem proving

candidates.description: We’re now accepting applications for the next cohort of OpenAI Fellows, a program which offers a compensated 6-month apprenticeship in AI research at OpenAI.
candidates.title: OpenAI Fellows Fall 2018

candidates.description: We’re releasing the full version of Gym Retro, a platform for reinforcement learning research on games. This brings our publicly-released game count from around 70 Atari games and 30 Sega games to over 1,000 games across a variety of backing emulators. We’re also releasing the tool we use to add new games to the platform.
candidates.title: Gym Retro

candidates.description: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012, the amount of compute used in the largest AI training runs has been increasing exponentially with a 3.4-month doubling time (by comparison, Moore’s Law had a 2-year doubling period)[^footnote-correction]. Since 2012, this metric has grown by more than 300,000x (a 2-year doubling period would yield only a 7x increase). Improvements in compute have been a key component of AI progress, so as long as this trend continues, it’s worth preparing for the implications of systems far outside today’s capabilities.
candidates.title: AI and compute

candidates.description: We’re proposing an AI safety technique which trains agents to debate topics with one another, using a human to judge who wins.
candidates.title: AI safety via debate

candidates.description: We’re releasing an experimental metalearning approach called Evolved Policy Gradients, a method that evolves the loss function of learning agents, which can enable fast training on novel tasks. Agents trained with EPG can succeed at basic tasks at test time that were outside their training regime, like learning to navigate to an object on a different side of the room from where it was placed during training.
candidates.title: Evolved Policy Gradients
Gotta Learn Fast: A new benchmark for generalization in RL

candidates.description: We’re launching a transfer learning contest that measures a reinforcement learning algorithm’s ability to generalize from previous experience.
candidates.title: Retro Contest
Variance reduction for policy gradient with action-dependent factorized baselines
Improving GANs using optimal transport

candidates.description: On March 3rd, we hosted our first hackathon with 100 members of the artificial intelligence community.
candidates.title: Report from the OpenAI hackathon
On first-order meta-learning algorithms

candidates.description: We’ve developed a simple meta-learning algorithm called Reptile which works by repeatedly sampling a task, performing stochastic gradient descent on it, and updating the initial parameters towards the final parameters learned on that task. Reptile is the application of the Shortest Descent algorithm to the meta-learning setting, and is mathematically similar to first-order MAML (which is a version of the well-known MAML algorithm) that only needs black-box access to an optimizer such as SGD or Adam, with similar computational efficiency and performance.
candidates.title: Reptile: A scalable meta-learning algorithm

candidates.description: We’re providing 6–10 stipends and mentorship to individuals from underrepresented groups to study deep learning full-time for 3 months and open-source a project.
candidates.title: OpenAI Scholars
Some considerations on learning to explore via meta-reinforcement learning
Multi-Goal Reinforcement Learning: Challenging robotics environments and request for research

candidates.description: We’re releasing eight simulated robotics environments and a Baselines implementation of Hindsight Experience Replay, all developed for our research over the past year. We’ve used these environments to train models which work on physical robots. We’re also releasing a set of requests for robotics research.
candidates.title: Ingredients for robotics research

candidates.description: Come to OpenAI’s office in San Francisco’s Mission District for talks and a hackathon on Saturday, March 3rd.
candidates.title: OpenAI hackathon

candidates.description: We’ve co-authored a paper that forecasts how malicious actors could misuse AI technology, and potential ways we can prevent and mitigate these threats. This paper is the outcome of almost a year of sustained work with our colleagues at the Future of Humanity Institute, the Centre for the Study of Existential Risk, the Center for a New American Security, the Electronic Frontier Foundation, and others.
candidates.title: Preparing for malicious uses of AI

candidates.description: We’re excited to welcome new donors to OpenAI.
candidates.title: OpenAI supporters

candidates.description: We’ve designed a method that encourages AIs to teach each other with examples that also make sense to humans. Our approach automatically selects the most informative examples to teach a concept—for instance, the best images to describe the concept of dogs—and experimentally we found our approach to be effective at teaching both AIs
candidates.title: Interpretable machine learning through teaching

candidates.description: We’ve built a system for automatically figuring out which object is meant by a word by having a neural network decide if the word belongs to each of about 100 automatically-discovered “types” (non-exclusive categories).
candidates.title: Discovering types for entity disambiguation

candidates.description: We’re releasing a new batch of seven unsolved problems which have come up in the course of our research at OpenAI.
candidates.title: Requests for Research 2.0
Scaling Kubernetes to 2,500 nodes

candidates.description: We’re releasing highly-optimized GPU kernels for an underexplored class of neural network architectures: networks with block-sparse weights. Depending on the chosen sparsity, these kernels can run orders of magnitude faster than cuBLAS or cuSPARSE. We’ve used them to attain state-of-the-art results in text sentiment analysis and generative modeling of text and images.
candidates.title: Block-sparse GPU kernels
Learning sparse neural networks through L₀ regularization
Interpretable and pedagogical examples

candidates.description: We’ve developed a hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm that learns high-level actions useful for solving a range of tasks, allowing fast solving of tasks requiring thousands of timesteps. Our algorithm, when applied to a set of navigation problems, discovers a set of high-level actions for walking and crawling in different directions, which enables the agent to master new navigation tasks quickly.
candidates.title: Learning a hierarchy

candidates.description: Our latest robotics techniques allow robot controllers, trained entirely in simulation and deployed on physical robots, to react to unplanned changes in the environment as they solve simple tasks. That is, we’ve used these techniques to build closed-loop systems rather than open-loop ones as before.
candidates.title: Generalizing from simulation
Sim-to-real transfer of robotic control with dynamics randomization
Asymmetric actor critic for image-based robot learning
Domain randomization and generative models for robotic grasping

candidates.description: We show that for the task of simulated robot wrestling, a meta-learning agent can learn to quickly defeat a stronger non-meta-learning agent, and also show that the meta-learning agent can adapt to physical malfunction.
candidates.title: Meta-learning for wrestling

candidates.description: We’ve found that self-play allows simulated AIs to discover physical skills like tackling, ducking, faking, kicking, catching, and diving for the ball, without explicitly designing an environment with these skills in mind. Self-play ensures that the environment is always the right difficulty for an AI to improve. Taken alongside our Dota 2 self-play results, we have increasing confidence that self-play will be a core part of powerful AI systems in the future.
candidates.title: Competitive self-play
Nonlinear computation in deep linear networks

candidates.description: We’re releasing an algorithm which accounts for the fact that other agents are learning too, and discovers self-interested yet collaborative strategies like tit-for-tat in the iterated prisoner’s dilemma. This algorithm, Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness (LOLA), is a small step towards agents that model other minds.
candidates.title: Learning to model other minds
Learning with opponent-learning awareness

candidates.description: We’re releasing two new OpenAI Baselines implementations: ACKTR and A2C. A2C is a synchronous, deterministic variant of Asynchronous Advantage Actor Critic (A3C) which we’ve found gives equal performance. ACKTR is a more sample-efficient reinforcement learning algorithm than TRPO and A2C, and requires only slightly more computation than A2C per update.
candidates.title: OpenAI Baselines: ACKTR & A2C

candidates.description: Our Dota 2 result shows that self-play can catapult the performance of machine learning systems from far below human level to superhuman, given sufficient compute. In the span of a month, our system went from barely matching a high-ranked player to beating the top pros and has continued to improve since then. Supervised deep learning systems can only be as good as their training datasets, but in self-play systems, the available data improves automatically as the agent gets better.
candidates.title: More on Dota 2

candidates.description: We’ve created a bot which beats the world’s top professionals at 1v1 matches of Dota 2 under standard tournament rules. The bot learned the game from scratch by self-play, and does not use imitation learning or tree search. This is a step towards building AI systems which accomplish well-defined goals in messy, complicated situations involving real humans.
candidates.title: Dota 2

candidates.description: RL-Teacher is an open-source implementation of our interface to train AIs via occasional human feedback rather than hand-crafted reward functions. The underlying technique was developed as a step towards safe AI systems, but also applies to reinforcement learning problems with rewards that are hard to specify.
candidates.title: Gathering human feedback

candidates.description: We’ve found that adding adaptive noise to the parameters of reinforcement learning algorithms frequently boosts performance. This exploration method is simple to implement and very rarely decreases performance, so it’s worth trying on any problem.
candidates.title: Better exploration with parameter noise

candidates.description: We’re releasing a new class of reinforcement learning algorithms, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which perform comparably or better than state-of-the-art approaches while being much simpler to implement and tune. PPO has become the default reinforcement learning algorithm at OpenAI because of its ease of use and good performance.
candidates.title: Proximal Policy Optimization

candidates.description: We’ve created images that reliably fool neural network classifiers when viewed from varied scales and perspectives. This challenges a claim from last week that self-driving cars would be hard to trick maliciously since they capture images from multiple scales, angles, perspectives, and the like.
candidates.title: Robust adversarial inputs
Hindsight Experience Replay
Teacher–student curriculum learning

candidates.description: We’re open-sourcing a high-performance Python library for robotic simulation using the MuJoCo engine, developed over our past year of robotics research.
candidates.title: Faster physics in Python

candidates.description: One step towards building safe AI systems is to remove the need for humans to write goal functions, since using a simple proxy for a complex goal, or getting the complex goal a bit wrong, can lead to undesirable and even dangerous behavior. In collaboration with DeepMind’s safety team, we’ve developed an algorithm which can infer what humans want by being told which of two proposed behaviors is better.
candidates.title: Learning from human preferences

candidates.description: Multiagent environments where agents compete for resources are stepping stones on the path to AGI. Multiagent environments have two useful properties: first, there is a natural curriculum—the difficulty of the environment is determined by the skill of your competitors (and if you’re competing against clones of yourself, the environment exactly matches your skill level). Second, a multiagent environment has no stable equilibrium: no matter how smart an agent is, there’s always pressure to get smarter. These environments have a very different feel from traditional environments, and it’ll take a
candidates.title: Learning to cooperate, compete, and communicate
UCB exploration via Q-ensembles

candidates.description: We’re open-sourcing OpenAI Baselines, our internal effort to reproduce reinforcement learning algorithms with performance on par with published results. We’ll release the algorithms over upcoming months; today’s release includes DQN and three of its variants.
candidates.title: OpenAI Baselines: DQN

candidates.description: We’ve created a robotics system, trained entirely in simulation and deployed on a physical robot, which can learn a new task after seeing it done once.
candidates.title: Robots that learn

candidates.description: We are releasing Roboschool: open-source software for robot simulation, integrated with OpenAI Gym.
candidates.title: Roboschool
Equivalence between policy gradients and soft Q-learning
Stochastic Neural Networks for hierarchical reinforcement learning

candidates.description: We’ve developed an unsupervised system which learns an excellent representation of sentiment, despite being trained only to predict the next character in the text of Amazon reviews.
candidates.title: Unsupervised sentiment neuron

candidates.description: We’ve created the world’s first Spam-detecting AI trained entirely in simulation and deployed on a physical robot.
candidates.title: Spam detection in the physical world

candidates.description: We’ve discovered that evolution strategies (ES), an optimization technique that’s been known for decades, rivals the performance of standard reinforcement learning (RL) techniques on modern RL benchmarks (e.g. Atari/MuJoCo), while overcoming many of RL’s inconveniences.
candidates.title: Evolution strategies as a scalable alternative to reinforcement learning
One-shot imitation learning

candidates.description: We’re excited to support today’s launch of Distill, a new kind of journal aimed at excellent communication of machine learning results (novel or existing).
candidates.title: Distill

candidates.description: In this post we’ll outline new OpenAI research in which agents develop their own language.
candidates.title: Learning to communicate
Emergence of grounded compositional language in multi-agent populations
Prediction and control with temporal segment models
Third-person imitation learning

candidates.description: Adversarial examples are inputs to machine learning models that an attacker has intentionally designed to cause the model to make a mistake; they’re like optical illusions for machines. In this post we’ll show how adversarial examples work across different mediums, and will discuss why securing systems against them can be difficult.
candidates.title: Attacking machine learning with adversarial examples
Adversarial attacks on neural network policies

candidates.description: The OpenAI team is now 45 people. Together, we’re pushing the frontier of AI capabilities—whether by validating novel ideas, creating new software systems, or deploying machine learning on robots.
candidates.title: Team update
PixelCNN++: Improving the PixelCNN with discretized logistic mixture likelihood and other modifications

candidates.description: Reinforcement learning algorithms can break in surprising, counterintuitive ways. In this post we’ll explore one failure mode, which is where you misspecify your reward function.
candidates.title: Faulty reward functions in the wild

candidates.description: We’re releasing Universe, a software platform for measuring and training an AI’s general intelligence across the world’s supply of games, websites and other applications.
candidates.title: Universe
#Exploration: A study of count-based exploration for deep reinforcement learning

candidates.description: We’re working with Microsoft to start running most of our large-scale experiments on Azure.
candidates.title: OpenAI and Microsoft
On the quantitative analysis of decoder-based generative models
A connection between generative adversarial networks, inverse reinforcement learning, and energy-based models
RL²: Fast reinforcement learning via slow reinforcement learning
Variational lossy autoencoder
Extensions and limitations of the neural GPU
Semi-supervised knowledge transfer for deep learning from private training data

candidates.description: Last week we hosted over a hundred and fifty AI practitioners in our offices for our first self-organizing conference on machine learning.
candidates.title: Report from the self-organizing conference
Transfer from simulation to real world through learning deep inverse dynamics model

candidates.description: Deep learning is an empirical science, and the quality of a group’s infrastructure is a multiplier on progress. Fortunately, today’s open-source ecosystem makes it possible for anyone to build great deep learning infrastructure.
candidates.title: Infrastructure for deep learning

candidates.description: The latest information about the Unconference is now available at the Unconference wiki, which will be periodically updated with more information for attendees.
candidates.title: Machine Learning Unconference

candidates.description: We’ve hired more great people to help us achieve our goals. Welcome, everyone!
candidates.title: Team update

candidates.description: Impactful scientific work requires working on the right problems—problems which are not just interesting, but whose solutions matter.
candidates.title: Special projects

candidates.description: We (along with researchers from Berkeley and Stanford) are co-authors on today’s paper led by Google Brain researchers, Concrete Problems in AI Safety. The paper explores many research problems around ensuring that modern machine learning systems operate as intended.
candidates.title: Concrete AI safety problems

candidates.description: OpenAI’s mission is to build safe AI, and ensure AI’s benefits are as widely and evenly distributed as possible.
candidates.title: OpenAI technical goals

candidates.description: This post describes four projects that share a common theme of enhancing or using generative models, a branch of unsupervised learning techniques in machine learning. In addition to describing our work, this post will tell you a bit more about generative models: what they are, why they are important, and where they might be going.
candidates.title: Generative models
Adversarial training methods for semi-supervised text classification

candidates.description: We’d like to welcome the latest set of team members to OpenAI (and we’re still hiring!)
candidates.title: Team update

candidates.description: We’re releasing the public beta of OpenAI Gym, a toolkit for developing and comparing reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms. It consists of a growing suite of environments (from simulated robots to Atari games), and a site for comparing and reproducing results.
candidates.title: OpenAI Gym Beta

candidates.description: We have two more team updates.
candidates.title: Welcome, Pieter and Shivon!

candidates.description: We’ve had some fantastic people join over the past few months (and we’re still hiring). Welcome, everyone!
candidates.title: Team++
Weight normalization: A simple reparameterization to accelerate training of deep neural networks

candidates.description: OpenAI is a non-profit artificial intelligence research company. Our goal is to advance digital intelligence in the way that is most likely to benefit humanity as a whole, unconstrained by a need to generate financial return. Since our research is free from financial obligations, we can better focus on a positive human impact.

candidates.description: 이번 이슈브리프는 공공임대주택 거주가 청년의 혼인·출산 이행에 미치는 영향을 분석하고, 미혼 청년층의 주거지원 확대와 결혼·출산에 따른 주거면적 전환을 연계하는 생애주기형 공공임대주택 정책을 제안한다.
candidates.title: 공공임대주택 거주와 청년의 혼인·출산 이행: 생애주기 연계형 주거정책의 필요성

candidates.description: 이번 이슈브리프는 AI 추천에 대한 설명을 단순히 늘리는 것보다 추천에 활용된 데이터의 유형과 서비스 맥락, 이용자 특성을 고려한 적정한 정보 제공이 중요함을 실증적으로 제시하고, 이용자의 실질적인 이해와 선택권을 제고하기 위한 AI 추천 투명성 정책의 방향을 제안한다.
candidates.title: AI 추천의 투명성, ‘더 많은 설명’이 정답인가?

candidates.description: 이번 이슈브리프는 한국 정치의 승자독식 구조와 적대적 양극화를 완화하기 위해 3~5인 중대선거구제하에서 아일랜드식 순위선택투표제를 도입하고, 이를 통해 온건한 유권자의 선호와 다양한 정치적 선택이 보다 충실히 대표될 수 있도록 공천제도와 관련 법령의 개혁을 함께 추진할 것을 제안한다.
candidates.title: 국회의원 선거제도 개혁방안: 순위선택투표제로의 전환

candidates.description: 이번 이슈브리프는 기존 성장 모델의 한계를 극복하기 위해 선진국의 기술과 신흥국의 시장을 전략적으로 연결하는 ‘글로벌 산업 허브’로 전환하여 경제 영토를 확장하고 국내 산업을 고도화하는 새로운 국가 성장 전략을 제안한다.
candidates.title: 「글로벌 산업 허브」 전략: 피크 코리아를 넘어 경제 영토 확장의 길로

candidates.description: 이번 이슈브리프는 기후변화와 초고령사회가 맞물리며 취약계층과 지역사회의 재난 위험이 커지는 상황에서, 환경·복지 정책의 연계와 실질적인 이동·대피 지원체계 구축, 지역 특성을 반영한 맞춤형 방재 거버넌스를 통해 기후·재난 회복력을 강화해야 한다고 제언한다.
candidates.title: 초고령사회 기후·재난 회복력 국가 전략

candidates.description: 이번 이슈브리프는 수도권 집중과 공간 불균형 문제를 분석하고, '5극3특' 국가균형성장 전략이 성장에는 긍정적인 효과를 가져올 수 있지만 공간 균형을 보장하기에는 한계가 있음을 실증적으로 검토하며, 정책의 성공 조건과 과제를 제시한다.
candidates.title: 지역 공진화를 위한 공간 전략: 5극3특 전략은 성장을 키우지만 균형을 보장하지 않는다

candidates.description: 이번 이슈브리프는 한국의 초저출산이 '무자녀 증가'와 출산에 따른 여성의 경제적 부담이라는 구조적 변화와 맞물려 심화되고 있음을 분석하고, 저출산 문제 해결을 위해 근무여건 유연화와 돌봄 지원 확대를 중심으로 한 새로운 저출산 대응 방향을 제시한다.
candidates.title: 한국의 저출산과 근무여건 유연화의 필요성

candidates.description: 이번 이슈브리프는 2024년 비상계엄 경험이 한국인의 민주주의 인식에 미친 영향을 2024년과 2025년 전국 단위 민주주의 인식조사와 아시아 바로미터 서베이와의 비교를 통해 분석하고, 이러한 인식 변화의 의미와 향후 민주주의 시민교육 및 정치 참여 활성화를 위한 정책적 과제를 제시한다.
candidates.title: 한국인의 민주주의 인식: 계엄은 한국인의 민주주의 인식을 변화시켰는가?

candidates.description: 이번 이슈브리프는 경제안보 시대 한국 기업의 글로벌 공급망 구조와 취약성을 기업 단위에서 분석하고, 공급망 회복력 강화를 위한 정책 과제와 새로운 정책 방향을 제시한다.
candidates.title: 기업 공급망 세계화와 한국 경제의 새로운 과제

candidates.description: 본 이슈브리프는 2035 국가온실가스감축목표(NDC)를 산업 성장 전략으로 전환하기 위한 한국형 녹색전환(K-GX)의 비전을 제시하고, 탄소중립과 산업 경쟁력, 에너지 안보를 동시에 달성하기 위한 5+1 핵심 우선과제를 제안한다.

candidates.title: 대한민국의 강대국 전략: 지정학, 공급망, 혁신성장

candidates.description: 국가미래전략원 보고서 『한미원자력협정의 선진 개정』은 1956~2015년 협정의 구조와 한계를 분석하고, 2035년 개정 시 한국의 기술자립·에너지안보·비확산 수용성을 높이기 위한 농축·재처리 권한 확대, 실증 기반, 기술동맹 강화 전략을 제시한다.
candidates.title: [국가미래전략원 연구 TF]한미 원자력 협력 협정의 선진적 개정을 위한 기반 연구

candidates.description: 국가미래전략원 의료개혁 TF 결과보고서 『지속가능한 미래 의료개혁』은 고령화·지역격차·재정위기 등 한국 의료체계의 취약성을 진단하고, 공간·기능·시간 기반의 분석틀을 통해 거버넌스 개편, 지역의료 강화, 전담의사제·디지털 헬스 도입, 기후·감염병 대응 등 지속가능한 의료개혁 전략을 제시한다.
candidates.title: 의료개혁 TF 결과보고서 지속가능한 미래 의료개혁의 방안

candidates.description: 국가미래전략원 <한일협력 TF>가 연구한 『글로벌 대한민국의 새로운 한일협력』은 급변하는 세계 질서 속에서 한국이 직면한 복합적 도전 과제를 진단하고, 이를 극복하기 위한 전략적 해법으로서 한일협력의 방향과 구체적 정책 대안을 제시한다.
candidates.title: 글로벌 대한민국의 새로운 한일협력

candidates.description: 국가미래전략원 <경제안보 클러스터>의 "2023 경제안보 클러스터 보고서"는 세계 각국의 공급망 지배력을 측정하고, 단기적이고 즉각적인 대응이 필요한 과제로 전략산업 복원력 강화 프로그램 개발, 핵심 산업 분야의 기술 주권 강화, 공급망 의존도 다변화, 국제협력체계의 제도적 강화와 등을 제시한다.
candidates.title: 2023EconomicSecurityReport

candidates.description: 국가미래전략원 <미·중관계 TF>의 보고서는 미·중 경쟁 시대에 미국과 한국이 공동 대응 복원력을 구축하기 위한 전략을 구상한다.
candidates.title: 국가미래전략원 미·중 관계 TF 보고서 발간

candidates.description: 본 연구는 서울대학교 국가미래전략원 <글로벌 한국 클러스터>의 2차 연도 사업의 주요 성과를 종합적으로 분석한다.
candidates.title: 글로벌 한국 클러스터 2024년 보고서 『경제 번영을 위한 강대국 전략: 산업, 문화, 안보의 융합』
